sources.entry: Zoneminder - Closed-circuit television (CCTV) software application which supports IP, USB and Analog cameras. (Source Code) GPL-2.0 PHP/deb

summary.one_liner: ZoneMinder is an integrated CCTV and security camera surveillance application for Linux that captures, analyzes, records and monitors attached cameras.
summary.what_it_does: ZoneMinder is described as an integrated set of applications for capture, analysis, recording and monitoring of CCTV or security cameras attached to a Linux machine. The README says it is designed for distributions that support the Video For Linux (V4L) interface, has been tested with BTTV-card cameras and various USB cameras, and supports most IP network cameras. The README is mostly installation guidance: it lists packaged distributions (Ubuntu PPA, Debian, RHEL/CentOS and clones, Fedora, OpenSUSE, Mageia, Arch AUR, Gentoo) and a Docker option. It also documents a zmeditconfigdata.sh tool for package maintainers to change ConfigData.pm defaults. Contribution steps (fork, issue, branch, pull request) are described, and the README points to ReadtheDocs for distro-specific instructions.
use_cases: monitor CCTV cameras on a Linux machine
run a home or small business surveillance system
connect USB, analog or IP network cameras
detect motion and record events from camera feeds
how_to_run: Install from a distro package repository (recommended; see README list of Ubuntu PPA, Debian, Fedora, Arch AUR, etc.)
docker pull zoneminder/zoneminder  (official image, also at ghcr.io/zoneminder/zoneminder)
git clone the zmdockerfiles repo, cd zmdockerfiles
notable: Runs on Linux with Video For Linux (V4L) support for analog, USB and IP cameras
Official Docker images for amd64 and arm64 with pinned release tags and an optional event server (-es) variant
Packages maintained for many Linux distributions
zmeditconfigdata.sh lets package maintainers change default config values without patching source
caveats: README discourages building from source in favor of packages or Docker
Nightly dev Docker builds are not recommended for systems you rely on
Docs are hosted externally on ReadtheDocs and the project site; the README itself is brief
